question:
I have a problem with YAML validation. A dictionary value contains space and it causes a problem. My error message in airflow looks like this:

Executing following command:

dbt run --vars {"post_hook":"reset query_group","whatever":"else"}   
[0m12:28:39  The YAML provided in the --vars argument is not valid.

Error: Invalid value for '--vars': String '{"post_hook":"reset' is not valid YAML

Actually when I run this in my command line (git bash) it works without errors. It's only a problem when run on airflow. How can I escape this?

I tried single quote like this:

dbt run --vars '{"post_hook":"reset query_group","whatever":"else"}'

I tried double quote as well:

dbt run --vars "{post_hook:'reset query_group',run_elementary:True}"

EDIT: See this partial answer for further investigation into this issue.

tl;dr: The DBT command is passed as a string argument to a shell script.
title: YAML passed as a variable in dbt command in airflow/shell script
answer:
You can use eval for this case :

Airflow script.sh

#!/bin/bash
echo "\$1 : $1"
eval "$1"

test with :

./script.sh "dbt run --vars '{\"post_hook\":\"reset query_group\",\"whatever\":\"else\"}'"

If you have the possibility to pass multiple strings to Airflow script, then you can avoid the use of eval by defining Airflow script2.sh

#!/bin/bash
echo "\$@ : $@"
"$@"

test with :

./script2.sh dbt run --vars '{"post_hook":"reset query_group","whatever":"else"}'
